revisions.title: TEE Security Handbook: practical verification, failure analysis and recovery for Ethereum
revisions.summary: Expand Bluethroat Labs' existing TEE Security Handbook with four reviewed engineering chapters, reusable security checklists and runnable examples. The work covers attestation verification, malicious-host interfaces, state recovery, and verification from source code to deployment. Funding also supports maintenance and documented use by independent Ethereum-facing teams.

sections.why:
Ethereum teams increasingly use TEEs for proving, signing and confidential execution. They need to establish more than whether an attestation has a valid signature: whether the workload is authorized, whether its inputs and host interfaces are safe, whether recovered state is current, and whether the deployed binary corresponds to reviewed source. The Handbook already explains TEE architectures and common failures; this expansion turns those foundations into checks engineers can execute.

[Taiko's postmortem](https://paragraph.com/@taiko-labs/taiko-security-incident-a-postmortem-and-next-steps) documents a debug-policy gap. Bluethroat's [published dstack research](https://bluethroatlabs.com/reveries/missing-tcb-status-check) addresses missing TCB-status enforcement. These cases demonstrate why authentic hardware evidence and safe application policy are separate concerns. The proposed chapters connect public incident analysis to rejection tests, review checklists and recovery exercises that Ethereum developers can apply to their own systems.
sections.in_scope:
- **Verifier engineering:** a practical acceptance-policy chapter covering debug state, measurements, TCB policy, collateral, freshness, key binding and failure behavior, with good/bad verification fixtures.
- **Malicious-host interfaces:** a casebook chapter covering concrete failures in host-controlled inputs or enclave interfaces, with an attacker-to-impact trace and vulnerable/fixed teaching example.
- **State continuity and recovery:** a chapter and exercise distinguishing authenticated storage, rollback, cloning, revocation and recovery after loss of the original host.
- **Source-to-deployment verification:** a pinned build walkthrough connecting reviewed source and build inputs to an attested deployment measurement, including an intentional mismatch.
- Four associated review checklists, independent review records, contribution/version records, corrections and six monthly maintenance updates.
- Documented use of the materials by independent Ethereum-facing teams, with a public evidence index and feedback-driven corrections.

The case material will draw on published Bluethroat research, cleared Secret Network lessons and public incident reports. Taiko is an initial verification-policy example. [Base Azul](https://blog.base.dev/introducing-base-azul) is a relevant comparison for proof-path and fallback assumptions. Any conclusion about a named implementation will identify the version and supporting evidence.

The planning allocation is $9,000 for Rahul's technical work, $4,000 for Wehi's research and writing, $4,000 for independent technical and milestone review, and $1,000 for test infrastructure and publication. These allocations support the milestone outcomes; they are not payments to users for reporting adoption.
sections.out_scope:
- The corporate website redesign, other Bluethroat products and reimbursement for completed work.
- New vulnerability hunts or disclosure of confidential findings before clearance.
- A comprehensive audit, certification or security guarantee for every implementation discussed.
- A physical-hardware attack campaign or a commitment to cover the entire longer-term research backlog.
sections.team:
**Rahul Saxena**, founder of Bluethroat Labs and the [Handbook's maintainer](https://bluethroatlabs.com/docs/contributors), leads technical research, reproduction validation and final editorial review. Phala's [security update](https://phala.com/posts/dstack-security-update-attestation-pipeline-hardening) publicly credits Rahul and Bluethroat for attestation-pipeline research and remediation collaboration.

**Wehi**, a Bluethroat Labs research intern, supports evidence collection, drafts, teaching examples and contribution records under Rahul's technical review. Funded contributions will be attributed in the public repository and release records.

Rahul operates the proposed recipient. Bluethroat has conducted security research involving Secret Network and collaborated on disclosures involving Phala/dstack. Existing Handbook contributors, including people identified on its contributors page as Coinbase-affiliated, are credited for past work; this proposal does not claim new participation or endorsement from them or their employers. The Handbook has been self-funded to date, and no external funding is committed to this proposed cycle. An independent technical reviewer will be appointed through the grant process; no reviewer is represented as already committed.
sections.why_grant:
The [public Handbook](https://bluethroatlabs.com/docs/executive-summary) already contains platform explanations, a Nitro workflow, implementation failure patterns and layered defenses. Bluethroat maintains that material and has published relevant original security research. The grant builds on an existing resource and delivery team instead of paying to establish one from scratch.

The Docusaurus migration is scheduled for September 16, 2026 and remains planned at submission. It will support version history, attributed contributions and an open contribution workflow. Existing content and that migration are not charged as new grant deliverables. The linked GitHub repository is the current website source; the migrated Handbook will identify its canonical content repository and licensing at publication.
sections.commitments:
- **Open materials:** new grant-funded prose will be published under CC BY 4.0 and original example code under MIT. Third-party material retains its own license and attribution; existing contributions will not be relicensed without permission.
- **Deliverables:** at least 4 substantial engineering chapters, 4 associated checklists and 4 runnable examples or verification-fixture collections. Every chapter records author, reviewer, last-verified date, relevant revisions, evidence and limitations.
- **Maintenance:** Rahul remains lead maintainer. Six dated maintenance records will cover corrections, issues and releases during the grant. Afterward, Bluethroat will keep published releases publicly accessible and continue maintenance from its own capacity; further expansion depends on internal resources or additional funding. There is no committed follow-on sponsor or paid subscription model.
- **Adoption:** at least 6 independent Ethereum-facing teams document real use, with at least 2 publishing a follow-up after 30 days. No adopters are claimed as already committed.
- **Accountability:** each paid milestone has public evidence and an independent review record. Examples distinguish teaching simulations from hardware reproduction, and all security claims preserve their attacker assumptions.

milestones.name: Verifier engineering and malicious-host interfaces
criteria: At least 2 engineering chapters are published in a versioned Handbook release, covering verifier acceptance policy and malicious-host interfaces, with source links, attacker assumptions and Ethereum applicability.
At least 2 associated checklists are published, each specifying the evidence a reviewer should collect for its checks.
A public repository contains a runnable verifier-fixture collection and a vulnerable/fixed host-interface teaching example, with pinned dependencies, commands and recorded results.
The verifier fixtures include rejection of an authentic but policy-unacceptable report; the host-interface example demonstrates both the failed invariant and its correction in public test output.
A reviewer outside the delivery team publishes a review record, with each issue linked to its correction or documented resolution.

milestones.name: Recovery and source-to-deployment verification
criteria: At least 2 further engineering chapters and 2 associated checklists are published, covering state continuity/recovery and source-to-deployment verification.

A public recovery exercise records behavior under restored storage, concurrent instances and loss of the original service instance, and identifies the state authority and backups needed for authorized recovery.
A public build walkthrough pins source, toolchain and dependencies, derives a deployment measurement, compares it with attestation evidence and records an intentional mismatch.
Public reproduction records distinguish simulation from hardware runs and identify the platform, versions, commands, expected outputs and limitations of both exercises.
An independent review record and issue-resolution links are published for both chapters and their artifacts.
At least 6 dated monthly maintenance records are published, listing corrections, reviewed issues and releases, or explicitly recording no changes for that month.

milestones.name: Documented use by Ethereum teams
criteria: At least 6 independent Ethereum-facing teams publicly confirm applying at least 1 funded checklist or artifact in an actual engineering or security-review workflow, with a dated record identifying the material's version, the check performed and its effect on a decision or review.

A public evidence index links each confirmation and identifies the distinct team behind it; Bluethroat staff, duplicate teams, automated activity, internal demonstrations and paid testimonials are excluded, and the independent milestone reviewer publishes validation of the count.
At least 2 counted teams publish a follow-up at least 30 days after their first recorded use, identifying continued use or a subsequent engineering decision informed by the material.
A public feedback log links counted users' feedback to Handbook corrections or documented editorial decisions.

A public evidence index links each confirmation and identifies the distinct team behind it; Bluethroat staff, duplicate teams, automated activity, internal demonstrations and paid testimonials are excluded, and the independent milestone reviewer publishes validation of the count.
At least 2 counted teams publish a follow-up at least 30 days after their first recorded use, identifying continued use or a subsequent engineering decision informed by the material.
A public feedback log links counted users' feedback to Handbook corrections or documented editorial decisions.

revisions.title: Trustblock: every public Ethereum and L2 audit tied to the contracts and commit it reviewed, free to look up
revisions.summary: Trustblock indexes over 10,800 public audit reports from 60 security firms and shows them in an audit card on 26 block explorers, including Etherscan, and on Blockscout. This grant ties every Ethereum and L2 report to the repo, commit and deployed addresses it names, and makes every record free to look up on public pages and through a free API. For the 100 largest Ethereum and L2 protocols it closes the coverage gaps and shows, for each core contract, whether the live code matches the audited commit and who can upgrade it. Anyone about to sign, list collateral or integrate can then see which public report named that exact contract, with each finding in the firm's own words.

sections.why:
- Users and protocols lose money to code nobody reviewed. ack3's H1 2026 incident dataset (Gattermayer, Kalivoda and Bašović, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13792) covers 135 DeFi incidents in the first half of 2026. Of the 68 where a pre-incident audit was found, 46 were hit through code outside every audit's scope, and out-of-scope paths account for 94.4% of those 68 incidents' losses.
- An "audited" badge does not say which contracts a report covered. That answer sits in PDFs on 60 firm websites, each with its own words for severity and status, and new reports appear every week.
- On Trustblock today, fewer than half of all reports name a deployed contract address (46.5%), and only about 1 in 5 protocol audits do (18.4%, 1,225 of 6,644). Many name a repository instead, so the link from a report to the live contract has to be made, and kept current: a report missing for three months is a gap a user cannot see.
- Every effort that compares deployed code with audits needs the same input first: which report reviewed which commit, which files and which addresses. This grant produces that input for every public Ethereum and L2 audit and makes it free to look up, record by record.
- Afterwards, a wallet user about to sign, a risk team listing collateral or an explorer visitor can look up which public reports named this exact contract and commit, with each finding's severity and status as the firm wrote it, or see that no report names it. Every record links to the firm's own PDF, so anyone can check it.
sections.in_scope:
- Ethereum mainnet, and L2s holding at least $200 million on L2BEAT at the start date.
- Repo, commit and deployed addresses extracted from every Ethereum and L2 report on Trustblock and linked to the contracts, each marked "named in report" or "confirmed by firm".
- Every Ethereum and L2 record free to look up on public pages and through the free API tier, with a documented field format and a dated weekly log of what was added.
- Missing public reports added for the 100 largest Ethereum and L2 DeFi protocols by TVL, and for each of their core contracts (the deployed contracts the protocol lists in its own documentation): the verified source compared with the audited commit (matches, differs with the changed files listed, or not verifiable), who can upgrade it (proxy admin, owner, multisig signers and threshold, timelock), and every upgrade since the audit.
- Six months of upkeep: every new public report from the indexed firms on an Ethereum or L2 project read twice, checked, pinned and added, and the card and API kept answering.
sections.out_scope:
- Alt-L1s and non-EVM chains, even where Trustblock covers them.
- Rebuilding contracts from source to compare bytecode, and the deployed-code comparison for protocols beyond the 100 largest.
- Reviewing or auditing code.
- Ranking, scoring or endorsing firms or protocols, or any statement that a contract carries no risk.
sections.team:
- Bilel Seddik, CEO of Trustblock: product, data and partnerships (https://x.com/0xBilel).
- Reports arrive two ways: firms with verified accounts publish through the dashboard or the API, and Trustblock indexes the rest from firms' public sites and GitHub, attributed to the firm. No other funder pays for this scope.
- Relationships: Trustblock works with the security firms that publish on it, including Quantstamp, QuillAudits, Hacken, Zokyo, and ack3 (formerly Ackee Blockchain), whose incident dataset is cited above. Etherscan and Blockscout show Trustblock's card through their own integrations. None of them funds this work unless listed as a backer, and Trustblock does not rank or score firms.
sections.why_grant:
Already built, all public:
- A publishing platform for security firms: verified firm accounts publish reports, scope and findings through a dashboard or the API. Today it holds over 10,800 public audit reports from 60 firms, on more than 7,200 projects: https://app.trustblock.run
- Contract-level data: about 22,000 deployed contract addresses tied to reports, and over 5,100 reports that name a deployed contract address.
- Report files kept on IPFS: about 3,900 reports are kept only as our pinned IPFS copy, so they stay readable when a firm's page moves or disappears.
- An audit card on the contract pages of 26 block explorers, including Etherscan, and on Blockscout: open the Cards tab of the Uniswap token link above.
- A reading pipeline: new reports are read twice, blind, and a finding goes in only when both readings agree on its severity and the firm's own status word ("Mitigated" stays "Mitigated"). A third reading settles any disagreement.
- A free API tier, embeds for firms and projects, public project, firm and audit pages, and a sitemap and llms.txt for search engines and AI agents.
- Grants delivered: Starknet Foundation (25,000 USDC, 2024; Starknet support shipped in January 2025) and AngelHack x Polygon (80,000 POL, 2025; three milestones reported complete in December 2025).
- The platform, the explorer integrations and the reading pipeline are already paid for. What costs money every month is the reading itself: following 60 firms' sites, reading each new PDF twice, checking it, and keeping the card and API answering. This grant pays for the scope pinning, six months of that reading work on Ethereum and L2, and the open release, at a fraction of what a build from scratch would cost.
sections.commitments:
- Access: every Ethereum and L2 record stays free to read on Trustblock's public pages and through the free API tier, each linked to the firm's own report. The platform's code is not part of this grant.
- Free use: the explorer card and the free API tier stay free for display partners and non-commercial users.
- Maintenance: anything that breaks in the records or the free lookups is fixed within 30 days through month 6. After that, the records stay free to look up for at least 24 months.
- Accuracy: each report is read twice, blind, and each firm's status word is kept as written. Where we cannot read it, the field is marked unchecked, never guessed. A blind check of 100 findings per firm is published for the 5 firms holding the most Ethereum and L2 audits.
- Signed statements by firms, where they exist, are shown next to the record.

milestones.name: Every Ethereum and L2 report pinned to its contracts and commit
criteria: A baseline list of the Ethereum and L2 reports on Trustblock is published at the start date. Every report on it carries the repo, commit and deployed addresses it names, linked to the contracts, or is marked "names none"; each value marked "named in report" or "confirmed by firm". The reviewer checks 30 random rows against the reports, at least 29 correct.

milestones.name: Every record free to look up
criteria: The pinned record (reports, contracts, commits, addresses, findings with severity and the firm's own status word) can be looked up by address, commit or report on public pages and through the free API tier, with a documented field format and the first weekly log; the reviewer looks up 20 rows.

milestones.name: The 100 largest protocols: coverage complete, deployed code matched to the audit
criteria: For the 100 largest Ethereum and L2 DeFi protocols by TVL (list fixed and published at the start date), at least 95% of the audit reports the indexed firms publish on their own sites are on Trustblock and pinned, with a before and after count file published.

For each of their core contracts, published: the verified source on Sourcify or the explorer compared with the audited commit (matches, differs with the changed files listed, or not verifiable, with the reason); who can upgrade it (proxy admin, owner, multisig signers and threshold, timelock); and every upgrade since the audit, dated. The reviewer re-runs the comparison and reads the upgrade rights onchain for 10 contracts.

milestones.name: Record kept current, months 1 to 3
criteria: At least 95% of the public reports the indexed firms publish for Ethereum or L2 projects in the period are on Trustblock within 14 days, read twice and pinned, with a dated weekly log of what was added; the reviewer checks 10 new reports against the log.

milestones.name: Record kept current, months 4 to 6
criteria: Same test for months 4 to 6, with the deployed-code comparison, upgrade rights and upgrade history re-run monthly for the 100 protocols; the reviewer checks 10 new reports against the log.

milestones.name: An outside team shows it before users act
criteria: At least 1 outside team shows the record to its users in production: a wallet or transaction-review tool, an explorer not showing Trustblock data at the start date, a security dataset or monitoring service, or the risk team of a protocol holding over $100 million onchain; live page or the team's written confirmation, checked by the reviewer.

milestones.name: Audit firms confirm their own scope
criteria: At least 8 audit firms beyond the start-date count confirm the scope of their own Ethereum or L2 reports on Trustblock ("confirmed by firm" marks on their records), at least 2 of them among the 20 firms holding the most Ethereum and L2 audits; the reviewer checks 4 firms.

revisions.title: Keep ETH InfraOps Open, Secure & Resilient: Validator Operation Standard Adoption Programme
revisions.summary:
ValOS (Validator Operations Standard) is an open-source security standard, risk and controls framework, and collection of best practices for secure and resilient Ethereum node operations. Developed with contributors across staking operations, exchanges, risk, cybersecurity and assurance, ValOS evolved through two community releases, the first in 2024 and the full standard in Sep 2026.

The ValOS Operational Adoption Programme (VOAP) will drive adoption across two parts of the Ethereum ecosystem:
- Staking: Node operators and staking pools use ValOS to assess and improve operational security, while staking protocols use ValOS evidence in operator oversight and decisions.
- Security & Assurance: Auditors, ratings providers, monitoring platforms, risk providers, and other security parties incorporate ValOS into their existing security services and products.

Over 18 months, VOAP will coordinate these efforts, targeting 12 organisations that demonstrably use and embed ValOS in their operations, products, services or decisions, with mechanisms to maintain security and resilience over time.

sections.why:
**ValOS is currently the only open-source standard for Ethereum validator operational security.** Other industry standards exist, but they restrict how people can use, modify or build upon them.

ValOS is free for anyone to adopt, adapt and extend, including for commercial use. This makes security controls accessible to more operators, while allowing auditors, monitoring platforms, ratings providers and other security companies to build their own tools and services to assess, monitor and improve infrastructure security.

**The ValOS standard has already been developed and gone through two rounds of updates and improvements. The next step is adoption.** The priority now is to put this work into practice, with organisations implementing security controls in their day-to-day operations to reduce risks, prevent failures and improve Ethereum infrastructure resilience.

**VOAP brings the same openness to adoption.** It helps operators implement ValOS security controls and security providers independently assess, monitor and support those practices. Together, they help ensure security improvements are not just documented, but implemented and maintained over time.

The programme will openly share adoption approaches, progress, challenges and lessons learned, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.

**Each adoption makes the next one easier.** Others can learn from what works, reuse proven security practices and build on previous work instead of starting from scratch. This allows security improvements made by one organisation to benefit others across Ethereum.

As more organisations adopt ValOS, their practical experience can also help improve the standard, keeping its security controls relevant as Ethereum infrastructure and risks evolve.

**The goal is not simply to have an open security standard, but to put it to work — building an open, community-driven security ecosystem where more operators implement stronger security controls, independent providers help maintain them, and shared learning makes Ethereum infrastructure safer and more resilient.**
sections.in_scope:
VOAP will deliver a coordinated, open adoption programme across Ethereum's staking and security and assurance ecosystems.

The programme will identify and develop adoption opportunities, recruit prospective adopters, facilitate ValOS integration into existing operations, products and services, and drive the ongoing application of security and resilience practices.

The work is organised into three areas.

**1. Staking Ecosystem: Implementing ValOS in Validator Operations**

VOAP will drive adoption among infrastructure operators and staking organisations through two pathways:

- **Self-assessment:** Recruit and support operators to assess their security practices against ValOS, identify gaps, apply relevant controls and declare their alignment with the standard, without requiring paid third-party certification.
- **Independent assessment:** Connect operators with qualified external assurance providers and facilitate access to ValOS-based independent assessments.

VOAP will also work with staking protocols, pools and institutional stakers to develop ways of incorporating ValOS assurance evidence into operator selection, oversight and incentives.

The objective is to embed ValOS into how Ethereum staking organisations assess, manage and continuously improve their operational security and resilience.

**2. Security & Assurance Ecosystem: Integrating ValOS into Security Services**

VOAP will drive adoption among organisations that assess, secure, monitor and support Ethereum validator infrastructure, across six areas:

- **Assurance & certification:** Integrate ValOS into independent security assessments, certification, control verification and ongoing assurance.
- **Ratings & risk intelligence:** Incorporate ValOS into validator security ratings, operator evaluations and risk analytics.
- **Security monitoring & detection:** Use ValOS risks and controls in monitoring, alerting and ongoing security oversight.
- **Infrastructure security technologies:** Build upon ValOS in validator security tooling, key management, distributed validator technology (DVT) and infrastructure protection services.
- **Incident response & resilience:** Incorporate ValOS into incident preparedness, response, recovery testing and operational resilience services.
- **Financial security & risk protection:** Use ValOS assurance evidence in underwriting, insurance, slashing protection and security-related risk decisions.

- **Document adoption work as it happens:** Share outreach approaches, integration methods, decisions, outcomes and lessons learned, including unsuccessful efforts, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.
- **Publish reusable adoption resources:** Make non-confidential integration examples, practical guidance and relevant materials openly available so other organisations can adapt and extend them.
- **Enable community participation and continuity:** Allow external contributors to propose opportunities, contribute improvements and continue adoption efforts using existing ValOS infrastructure, without depending on Lionscraft.

revisions.summary:
ValOS (Validator Operations Standard) is an open-source security standard, risk and controls framework, and collection of best practices for secure and resilient Ethereum node operations. Developed with contributors across staking operations, exchanges, risk, cybersecurity and assurance, ValOS evolved through two community releases, the first in 2024 and the full standard in Sep 2026.

The ValOS Operational Adoption Programme (VOAP) will drive adoption across two parts of the Ethereum ecosystem:
- Staking: Node operators and staking pools use ValOS to assess and improve operational security, while staking protocols use ValOS evidence in operator oversight and decisions.
- Security & Assurance: Auditors, ratings providers, monitoring platforms, risk providers, and other security parties incorporate ValOS into their existing security services and products.

Over 18 months, VOAP will coordinate these efforts, targeting 12 organisations that demonstrably use and embed ValOS in their operations, products, services or decisions, with mechanisms to maintain security and resilience over time.

revisions.title: Keep ETH InfraOps Open, Secure & Resilient: Validator Operation Standard Adoption Programme
revisions.summary:
ValOS (Validator Operations Standard) is an open-source security standard, risk and controls framework, and collection of best practices for secure and resilient Ethereum node operations. Developed with contributors across staking operations, exchanges, risk, cybersecurity and assurance, ValOS evolved through two community releases, the first in 2024 and the full standard in Sep 2026.

The ValOS Operational Adoption Programme (VOAP) will drive adoption across two parts of the Ethereum ecosystem:
- Staking: Node operators and staking pools use ValOS to assess and improve operational security, while staking protocols use ValOS evidence in operator oversight and decisions.
- Security & Assurance: Auditors, ratings providers, monitoring platforms, risk providers, and other security parties incorporate ValOS into their existing security services and products.

Over 18 months, VOAP will coordinate these efforts, targeting 12 organisations that demonstrably use and embed ValOS in their operations, products, services or decisions, with mechanisms to maintain security and resilience over time.

sections.why:
**ValOS is currently the only open-source standard for Ethereum validator operational security.** Other industry standards exist, but they restrict how people can use, modify or build upon them.

ValOS is free for anyone to adopt, adapt and extend, including for commercial use. This makes security controls accessible to more operators, while allowing auditors, monitoring platforms, ratings providers and other security companies to build their own tools and services to assess, monitor and improve infrastructure security.

**The ValOS standard has already been developed and gone through two rounds of updates and improvements. The next step is adoption.** The priority now is to put this work into practice, with organisations implementing security controls in their day-to-day operations to reduce risks, prevent failures and improve Ethereum infrastructure resilience.

**VOAP brings the same openness to adoption.** It helps operators implement ValOS security controls and security providers independently assess, monitor and support those practices. Together, they help ensure security improvements are not just documented, but implemented and maintained over time.

The programme will openly share adoption approaches, progress, challenges and lessons learned, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.

**Each adoption makes the next one easier.** Others can learn from what works, reuse proven security practices and build on previous work instead of starting from scratch. This allows security improvements made by one organisation to benefit others across Ethereum.

As more organisations adopt ValOS, their practical experience can also help improve the standard, keeping its security controls relevant as Ethereum infrastructure and risks evolve.

**The goal is not simply to have an open security standard, but to put it to work — building an open, community-driven security ecosystem where more operators implement stronger security controls, independent providers help maintain them, and shared learning makes Ethereum infrastructure safer and more resilient.**
sections.in_scope:
VOAP will deliver a coordinated, open adoption programme across Ethereum's staking and security and assurance ecosystems.

The programme will identify and develop adoption opportunities, recruit prospective adopters, facilitate ValOS integration into existing operations, products and services, and drive the ongoing application of security and resilience practices.

The work is organised into three areas.

**1. Staking Ecosystem: Implementing ValOS in Validator Operations**

VOAP will drive adoption among infrastructure operators and staking organisations through two pathways:

- **Self-assessment:** Recruit and support operators to assess their security practices against ValOS, identify gaps, apply relevant controls and declare their alignment with the standard, without requiring paid third-party certification.
- **Independent assessment:** Connect operators with qualified external assurance providers and facilitate access to ValOS-based independent assessments.

VOAP will also work with staking protocols, pools and institutional stakers to develop ways of incorporating ValOS assurance evidence into operator selection, oversight and incentives.

The objective is to embed ValOS into how Ethereum staking organisations assess, manage and continuously improve their operational security and resilience.

**2. Security & Assurance Ecosystem: Integrating ValOS into Security Services**

VOAP will drive adoption among organisations that assess, secure, monitor and support Ethereum validator infrastructure, across six areas:

- **Assurance & certification:** Integrate ValOS into independent security assessments, certification, control verification and ongoing assurance.
- **Ratings & risk intelligence:** Incorporate ValOS into validator security ratings, operator evaluations and risk analytics.
- **Security monitoring & detection:** Use ValOS risks and controls in monitoring, alerting and ongoing security oversight.
- **Infrastructure security technologies:** Build upon ValOS in validator security tooling, key management, distributed validator technology (DVT) and infrastructure protection services.
- **Incident response & resilience:** Incorporate ValOS into incident preparedness, response, recovery testing and operational resilience services.
- **Financial security & risk protection:** Use ValOS assurance evidence in underwriting, insurance, slashing protection and security-related risk decisions.

**Every VOAP-supported integration must address how security practices or assurance remain effective and relevant over time.** VOAP will make continuity a core requirement of its adoption partnerships, including suitable mechanisms for ongoing monitoring, periodic reviews, remediation follow-up or reassessment after material changes and incidents.

The specific mechanisms will be designed, implemented and maintained by the adopting organisations themselves.

The objective is to embed ValOS into the existing services and technologies that help Ethereum infrastructure prevent security failures, detect problems, respond, recover and improve.

**3. Open Adoption: Making Adoption Open, Collaborative and Reusable**

VOAP will operate as an **Open Adoption Programme**, allowing anyone in the Ethereum ecosystem to participate, propose adoption opportunities, contribute to integrations and build upon existing work.

VOAP will:

- **Maintain an open adoption register:** Publish opportunities, their proposed ValOS applications, progress, obstacles and next steps, so others can participate or pursue them independently.
- **Document adoption work as it happens:** Share outreach approaches, integration methods, decisions, outcomes and lessons learned, including unsuccessful efforts, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.
- **Publish reusable adoption resources:** Make non-confidential integration examples, practical guidance and relevant materials openly available so other organisations can adapt and extend them.
- **Enable community participation and continuity:** Allow external contributors to propose opportunities, contribute improvements and continue adoption efforts using existing ValOS infrastructure, without depending on Lionscraft.

**The result is an open, reusable body of adoption work that grows with each contribution.** Every adoption can make the next easier, while helping the Ethereum ecosystem independently expand, maintain and improve the use of ValOS.
sections.out_scope:
- Performing audits, security assessments or certification.
- Operating or securing third-party validator infrastructure.
- Building or maintaining partners' security products or services.
- Creating new assurance, ratings or certification standards.
- Routine ValOS governance, standards maintenance or publication of ValOS v2.
- Funding or administering existing Lido assessment subsidies.
- Adoption outside the Ethereum ecosystem.
sections.team:
**[Lionscraft](https://www.lionscraft.io/) has been the lead contributor, coordinator and maintainer of D.U.C.K. and subsequently ValOS since the initiative began in 2023.** Over nearly three years, Lionscraft has led the development, publication and ongoing improvement of the standard, its security controls, tools and best practices.

The initiative has involved contributions from 20 organisations across Ethereum staking, node operations, cybersecurity, risk and assurance. Lionscraft coordinated their participation, bringing together organisations with different expertise and levels of involvement. Some were major contributors to the standard and its supporting resources, while others provided specialist input, reviewed specific sections or contributed to individual controls and practices.

This experience is directly relevant to VOAP. Lionscraft has already demonstrated its ability to coordinate diverse independent organisations around a shared, open-source security framework, manage contributions and turn that collaboration into published outputs. **VOAP builds on this experience, shifting the focus from developing ValOS to driving its adoption across the Ethereum ecosystem.**
sections.why_grant:
**ValOS is the result of nearly three years of development and industry collaboration, originally initiated and funded through Lido.**

Beginning with D.U.C.K. in November 2023, the initiative evolved through two phases of development, delivering an open-source security standard, risk and controls framework, assessment resources, toolkits and best practices for Ethereum validator operations. - **An open-source standard:** Published security risks, controls, mitigation practices and assessment guidance, available for anyone to use, adapt and extend.
- **Tools and best practices:** Existing resources that support operators in assessing and improving their security and resilience.
- **Industry collaboration:** Contributions from 20 organisations across staking operations, exchanges, cybersecurity, risk and assurance.
- **An independent assessment pathway:** Qualified third-party assessors can evaluate operators against ValOS. Lido will also subsidise part of the assessment costs for four early-adopter node operators.

- **Independent assessment:** Connect operators with qualified external assurance providers and facilitate access to ValOS-based independent assessments.

VOAP will also work with staking protocols, pools and institutional stakers to develop ways of incorporating ValOS assurance evidence into operator selection, oversight and incentives.

The objective is to embed ValOS into how Ethereum staking organisations assess, manage and continuously improve their operational security and resilience.

**2. Security & Assurance Ecosystem: Integrating ValOS into Security Services**

VOAP will drive adoption among organisations that assess, secure, monitor and support Ethereum validator infrastructure, across six areas:

- **Assurance & certification:** Integrate ValOS into independent security assessments, certification, control verification and ongoing assurance.
- **Ratings & risk intelligence:** Incorporate ValOS into validator security ratings, operator evaluations and risk analytics.
- **Security monitoring & detection:** Use ValOS risks and controls in monitoring, alerting and ongoing security oversight.
- **Infrastructure security technologies:** Build upon ValOS in validator security tooling, key management, distributed validator technology (DVT) and infrastructure protection services.
- **Incident response & resilience:** Incorporate ValOS into incident preparedness, response, recovery testing and operational resilience services.
- **Financial security & risk protection:** Use ValOS assurance evidence in underwriting, insurance, slashing protection and security-related risk decisions.

**Every VOAP-supported integration must address how security practices or assurance remain effective and relevant over time.** VOAP will make continuity a core requirement of its adoption partnerships, including suitable mechanisms for ongoing monitoring, periodic reviews, remediation follow-up or reassessment after material changes and incidents.

The specific mechanisms will be designed, implemented and maintained by the adopting organisations themselves.

The objective is to embed ValOS into the existing services and technologies that help Ethereum infrastructure prevent security failures, detect problems, respond, recover and improve.

**3. Open Adoption: Making Adoption Open, Collaborative and Reusable**

VOAP will operate as an **Open Adoption Programme**, allowing anyone in the Ethereum ecosystem to participate, propose adoption opportunities, contribute to integrations and build upon existing work.

VOAP will:

- **Maintain an open adoption register:** Publish opportunities, their proposed ValOS applications, progress, obstacles and next steps, so others can participate or pursue them independently.
- **Document adoption work as it happens:** Share outreach approaches, integration methods, decisions, outcomes and lessons learned, including unsuccessful efforts, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.
- **Publish reusable adoption resources:** Make non-confidential integration examples, practical guidance and relevant materials openly available so other organisations can adapt and extend them.
- **Enable community participation and continuity:** Allow external contributors to propose opportunities, contribute improvements and continue adoption efforts using existing ValOS infrastructure, without depending on Lionscraft.

**The result is an open, reusable body of adoption work that grows with each contribution.** Every adoption can make the next easier, while helping the Ethereum ecosystem independently expand, maintain and improve the use of ValOS.
sections.out_scope:
- Performing audits, security assessments or certification.
- Operating or securing third-party validator infrastructure.
- Building or maintaining partners' security products or services.
- Creating new assurance, ratings or certification standards.
- Routine ValOS governance, standards maintenance or publication of ValOS v2.
- Funding or administering existing Lido assessment subsidies.
- Adoption outside the Ethereum ecosystem.
sections.team:
**[Lionscraft](https://www.lionscraft.io/) has been the lead contributor, coordinator and maintainer of D.U.C.K. and subsequently ValOS since the initiative began in 2023.** Over nearly three years, Lionscraft has led the development, publication and ongoing improvement of the standard, its security controls, tools and best practices.

The initiative has involved contributions from 20 organisations across Ethereum staking, node operations, cybersecurity, risk and assurance. Some were major contributors to the standard and its supporting resources, while others provided specialist input, reviewed specific sections or contributed to individual controls and practices.

This experience is directly relevant to VOAP. Lionscraft has already demonstrated its ability to coordinate diverse independent organisations around a shared, open-source security framework, manage contributions and turn that collaboration into published outputs. **VOAP builds on this experience, shifting the focus from developing ValOS to driving its adoption across the Ethereum ecosystem.**

Beginning with D.U.C.K. in November 2023, the initiative evolved through two phases of development, delivering an open-source security standard, risk and controls framework, assessment resources, toolkits and best practices for Ethereum validator operations. - **An open-source standard:** Published security risks, controls, mitigation practices and assessment guidance, available for anyone to use, adapt and extend.

milestones.name: Activate ValOS Adoption
criteria: Identify at least 20 qualified prospective adopters across Ethereum's staking and security and assurance ecosystems, each with a specific ValOS security or resilience application; the independent reviewer verifies prospect records.
Deliver individualised ValOS adoption approaches to organisations in the initial pool, identifying the application and next action; the reviewer verifies dated correspondence.

milestones.name: Drive Staking Ecosystem Adoption
criteria: Deliver at least 10 documented operator-specific adoption actions involving ValOS self-assessment, independent assessment or ongoing security and resilience practices; the independent reviewer inspects correspondence and activity records.

Deliver at least 6 tailored proposals to staking protocols, pools or institutional stakers explaining how ValOS evidence could inform operator oversight, selection or incentives; the reviewer verifies proposals and delivery records.

milestones.name: Drive Security & Assurance Ecosystem Adoption
criteria: Deliver at least 10 documented provider-specific adoption actions involving real ValOS applications in assurance, ratings, monitoring, infrastructure security or financial risk services; the independent reviewer checks correspondence and activity records.

Deliver at least 6 tailored provider proposals describing a specific ValOS integration, relevant security risks and a partner-owned mechanism for continued assessment, monitoring or review; the reviewer verifies delivery records.

milestones.name: Staking Ecosystem Operational Adoption — First 3 Operators
criteria: At least 3 independent Ethereum node operators, each running at least 20,000 ETH worth of mainnet validators, use ValOS through completed self-assessments or independent assessments
Each operator incorporates ValOS into its security-management processes and identifies responsibility for continued control review; the reviewer verifies the supporting records.

milestones.name: Security & Assurance Ecosystem Operational Adoption — Second set of 3 Providers
criteria: At least 6 total independent Ethereum node operators, each running at least 20,000 ETH worth of mainnet validators, use ValOS through completed self-assessments or independent assessments, at least 1 of them a Lido node operator

Each provider incorporates ValOS into a repeatable service process with a mechanism for continued review, monitoring or reassessment; the reviewer inspects operating evidence, confidentially where necessary.

milestones.name: Staking Ecosystem Operational Adoption — Third set of Operators
criteria: At least 9 total independent Ethereum node operators, each running at least 20,000 ETH worth of mainnet validators, use ValOS through completed self-assessments or independent assessments, at least 1 of them: Kiln, Figment, Chorus One, P2P, Everstake, Mavan or Coinbase.
Each operator incorporates ValOS into its security-management processes and identifies responsibility for continued control review; the reviewer verifies the supporting records.

milestones.name: Security & Assurance Ecosystem Operational Adoption — Fourth set of 3 Providers
criteria: At least 12 total independent Ethereum node operators, each running at least 20,000 ETH worth of mainnet validators, use ValOS through completed self-assessments or independent assessments, at least 3 of them Lido node operators and 2 of: Kiln, Figment, Chorus One, P2P, Everstake, Mavan or Coinbase.

Each provider incorporates ValOS into a repeatable service process with a mechanism for continued review, monitoring or reassessment; the reviewer inspects operating evidence, confidentially where necessary.

revisions.title: Keep ETH InfraOps Open, Secure & Resilient: Validator Operation Standard Adoption Programme
revisions.summary:
ValOS (Validator Operations Standard) is an open-source security standard, risk and controls framework, and collection of best practices for secure and resilient Ethereum node operations. Developed with contributors across staking operations, exchanges, risk, cybersecurity and assurance, ValOS evolved through two community releases, the first in 2024 and the full standard in Sep 2026.

The ValOS Operational Adoption Programme (VOAP) will drive adoption across two parts of the Ethereum ecosystem:
- Staking: Node operators and staking pools use ValOS to assess and improve operational security, while staking protocols use ValOS evidence in operator oversight and decisions.
- Security & Assurance: Auditors, ratings providers, monitoring platforms, risk providers, and other security parties incorporate ValOS into their existing security services and products.

Over 18 months, VOAP will coordinate these efforts, targeting 12 organisations that demonstrably use and embed ValOS in their operations, products, services or decisions, with mechanisms to maintain security and resilience over time.

revisions.title: Keep ETH InfraOps Open, Secure & Resilient: Validator Operation Standard Adoption Programme
revisions.summary:
ValOS (Validator Operations Standard) is an open-source security standard, risk and controls framework, and collection of best practices for secure and resilient Ethereum node operations. Developed with contributors across staking operations, exchanges, risk, cybersecurity and assurance, ValOS evolved through two community releases, the first in 2024 and the full standard in Sep 2026.

The ValOS Operational Adoption Programme (VOAP) will drive adoption across two parts of the Ethereum ecosystem:
- Staking: Node operators and staking pools use ValOS to assess and improve operational security, while staking protocols use ValOS evidence in operator oversight and decisions.
- Security & Assurance: Auditors, ratings providers, monitoring platforms, risk providers, and other security parties incorporate ValOS into their existing security services and products.

Over 18 months, VOAP will coordinate these efforts, targeting 12 organisations that demonstrably use and embed ValOS in their operations, products, services or decisions, with mechanisms to maintain security and resilience over time.

sections.why:
**ValOS is currently the only open-source standard for Ethereum validator operational security.** Other industry standards exist, but they restrict how people can use, modify or build upon them.

ValOS is free for anyone to adopt, adapt and extend, including for commercial use. This makes security controls accessible to more operators, while allowing auditors, monitoring platforms, ratings providers and other security companies to build their own tools and services to assess, monitor and improve infrastructure security.

**The ValOS standard has already been developed and gone through two rounds of updates and improvements. The next step is adoption.** The priority now is to put this work into practice, with organisations implementing security controls in their day-to-day operations to reduce risks, prevent failures and improve Ethereum infrastructure resilience.

**VOAP brings the same openness to adoption.** It helps operators implement ValOS security controls and security providers independently assess, monitor and support those practices. Together, they help ensure security improvements are not just documented, but implemented and maintained over time.

The programme will openly share adoption approaches, progress, challenges and lessons learned, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.

**Each adoption makes the next one easier.** Others can learn from what works, reuse proven security practices and build on previous work instead of starting from scratch. This allows security improvements made by one organisation to benefit others across Ethereum.

As more organisations adopt ValOS, their practical experience can also help improve the standard, keeping its security controls relevant as Ethereum infrastructure and risks evolve.

**The goal is not simply to have an open security standard, but to put it to work — building an open, community-driven security ecosystem where more operators implement stronger security controls, independent providers help maintain them, and shared learning makes Ethereum infrastructure safer and more resilient.**
sections.in_scope:
VOAP will deliver a coordinated, open adoption programme across Ethereum's staking and security and assurance ecosystems.

The programme will identify and develop adoption opportunities, recruit prospective adopters, facilitate ValOS integration into existing operations, products and services, and drive the ongoing application of security and resilience practices.

The work is organised into three areas.

**1. Staking Ecosystem: Implementing ValOS in Validator Operations**

VOAP will drive adoption among infrastructure operators and staking organisations through two pathways:

- **Self-assessment:** Recruit and support operators to assess their security practices against ValOS, identify gaps, apply relevant controls and declare their alignment with the standard, without requiring paid third-party certification.
- **Independent assessment:** Connect operators with qualified external assurance providers and facilitate access to ValOS-based independent assessments.

VOAP will also work with staking protocols, pools and institutional stakers to develop ways of incorporating ValOS assurance evidence into operator selection, oversight and incentives.

The objective is to embed ValOS into how Ethereum staking organisations assess, manage and continuously improve their operational security and resilience.

**2. Security & Assurance Ecosystem: Integrating ValOS into Security Services**

VOAP will drive adoption among organisations that assess, secure, monitor and support Ethereum validator infrastructure, across six areas:

- **Assurance & certification:** Integrate ValOS into independent security assessments, certification, control verification and ongoing assurance.
- **Ratings & risk intelligence:** Incorporate ValOS into validator security ratings, operator evaluations and risk analytics.
- **Security monitoring & detection:** Use ValOS risks and controls in monitoring, alerting and ongoing security oversight.
- **Infrastructure security technologies:** Build upon ValOS in validator security tooling, key management, distributed validator technology (DVT) and infrastructure protection services.
- **Incident response & resilience:** Incorporate ValOS into incident preparedness, response, recovery testing and operational resilience services.
- **Financial security & risk protection:** Use ValOS assurance evidence in underwriting, insurance, slashing protection and security-related risk decisions.

**Every VOAP-supported integration must address how security practices or assurance remain effective and relevant over time.** VOAP will make continuity a core requirement of its adoption partnerships, including suitable mechanisms for ongoing monitoring, periodic reviews, remediation follow-up or reassessment after material changes and incidents.

The specific mechanisms will be designed, implemented and maintained by the adopting organisations themselves.

The objective is to embed ValOS into the existing services and technologies that help Ethereum infrastructure prevent security failures, detect problems, respond, recover and improve.

**3. Open Adoption: Making Adoption Open, Collaborative and Reusable**

VOAP will operate as an **Open Adoption Programme**, allowing anyone in the Ethereum ecosystem to participate, propose adoption opportunities, contribute to integrations and build upon existing work.

VOAP will:

- **Maintain an open adoption register:** Publish opportunities, their proposed ValOS applications, progress, obstacles and next steps, so others can participate or pursue them independently.
- **Document adoption work as it happens:** Share outreach approaches, integration methods, decisions, outcomes and lessons learned, including unsuccessful efforts, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.
- **Publish reusable adoption resources:** Make non-confidential integration examples, practical guidance and relevant materials openly available so other organisations can adapt and extend them.
- **Enable community participation and continuity:** Allow external contributors to propose opportunities, contribute improvements and continue adoption efforts using existing ValOS infrastructure, without depending on Lionscraft.

**The result is an open, reusable body of adoption work that grows with each contribution.** Every adoption can make the next easier, while helping the Ethereum ecosystem independently expand, maintain and improve the use of ValOS.
sections.out_scope:
- Performing audits, security assessments or certification.
- Operating or securing third-party validator infrastructure.
- Building or maintaining partners' security products or services.
- Creating new assurance, ratings or certification standards.
- Routine ValOS governance, standards maintenance or publication of ValOS v2.
- Funding or administering existing Lido assessment subsidies.
- Adoption outside the Ethereum ecosystem.
sections.team:
**[Lionscraft](https://www.lionscraft.io/) has been the lead contributor, coordinator and maintainer of D.U.C.K. and subsequently ValOS since the initiative began in 2023.** Over nearly three years, Lionscraft has led the development, publication and ongoing improvement of the standard, its security controls, tools and best practices.

The initiative has involved contributions from 20 organisations across Ethereum staking, node operations, cybersecurity, risk and assurance. Lionscraft coordinated their participation, bringing together organisations with different expertise and levels of involvement. Some were major contributors to the standard and its supporting resources, while others provided specialist input, reviewed specific sections or contributed to individual controls and practices.

This experience is directly relevant to VOAP. Lionscraft has already demonstrated its ability to coordinate diverse independent organisations around a shared, open-source security framework, manage contributions and turn that collaboration into published outputs. **VOAP builds on this experience, shifting the focus from developing ValOS to driving its adoption across the Ethereum ecosystem.**

**The ValOS standard has already been developed and gone through two rounds of updates and improvements. The next step is adoption.** The priority now is to put this work into practice, with organisations implementing security controls in their day-to-day operations to reduce risks, prevent failures and improve Ethereum infrastructure resilience.

**VOAP brings the same openness to adoption.** It helps operators implement ValOS security controls and security providers independently assess, monitor and support those practices. Together, they help ensure security improvements are not just documented, but implemented and maintained over time.

The programme will openly share adoption approaches, progress, challenges and lessons learned, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.

**Each adoption makes the next one easier.** Others can learn from what works, reuse proven security practices and build on previous work instead of starting from scratch. This allows security improvements made by one organisation to benefit others across Ethereum.

As more organisations adopt ValOS, their practical experience can also help improve the standard, keeping its security controls relevant as Ethereum infrastructure and risks evolve.

sections.in_scope:
VOAP will deliver a coordinated, open adoption programme across Ethereum's staking and security and assurance ecosystems.

The programme will identify and develop adoption opportunities, recruit prospective adopters, facilitate ValOS integration into existing operations, products and services, and drive the ongoing application of security and resilience practices.

VOAP will prioritise adoption opportunities with credible implementation pathways, meaningful security benefits and the potential for wider ecosystem adoption.

The work is organised into three areas.

**1. Staking Ecosystem: Implementing ValOS in Validator Operations**

VOAP will drive adoption among infrastructure operators and staking organisations through two pathways:

- **Self-assessment:** Recruit and support operators to assess their security practices against ValOS, identify gaps, apply relevant controls and declare their alignment with the standard, without requiring paid third-party certification.
- **Independent assessment:** Connect operators with qualified external assurance providers and facilitate access to ValOS-based independent assessments.

VOAP will target operators of different sizes and staking affiliations, supporting adoption across the wider Ethereum staking ecosystem.

VOAP will also selectively engage staking protocols, pools and institutional stakers where there are credible opportunities to incorporate ValOS assurance evidence into operator selection, oversight and incentives.

The objective is to embed ValOS into how Ethereum staking organisations assess, manage and continuously improve their operational security and resilience.

**2. Security & Assurance Ecosystem: Integrating ValOS into Security Services**

VOAP will drive adoption among organisations that assess, secure, monitor and support Ethereum validator infrastructure. Potential adoption areas include:

- **Assurance & certification:** Integrate ValOS into independent security assessments, certification, control verification and ongoing assurance.
- **Ratings & risk intelligence:** Incorporate ValOS into validator security ratings, operator evaluations and risk analytics.
- **Security monitoring & detection:** Use ValOS risks and controls in monitoring, alerting and ongoing security oversight.
- **Infrastructure security technologies:** Build upon ValOS in validator security tooling, key management, distributed validator technology (DVT) and infrastructure protection services.
- **Incident response & resilience:** Incorporate ValOS into incident preparedness, response, recovery testing and operational resilience services.
- **Financial security & risk protection:** Use ValOS assurance evidence in underwriting, insurance, slashing protection and security-related risk decisions.

VOAP will prioritise integration opportunities based on their implementation feasibility, security impact and potential to extend the benefits of ValOS across multiple Ethereum infrastructure operators.

**Every VOAP-supported integration must address how security practices or assurance remain effective and relevant over time.** VOAP will make continuity a core requirement of its adoption partnerships, including suitable mechanisms for ongoing monitoring, periodic reviews, remediation follow-up or reassessment after material changes and incidents.

The specific mechanisms will be designed, implemented and maintained by the adopting organisations themselves.

The objective is to embed ValOS into the existing services and technologies that help Ethereum infrastructure prevent security failures, detect problems, respond, recover and improve.

**3. Open Adoption: Making Adoption Open, Collaborative and Reusable**

VOAP will operate as an **Open Adoption Programme**, allowing anyone in the Ethereum ecosystem to participate, propose adoption opportunities, contribute to integrations and build upon existing work.

VOAP will:

- **Maintain an open adoption register:** Publish opportunities, their proposed ValOS applications, progress, obstacles and next steps, so others can participate or pursue them independently.
- **Document adoption work as it happens:** Share outreach approaches, integration methods, decisions, outcomes and lessons learned, including unsuccessful efforts, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.
- **Publish reusable adoption resources:** Make non-confidential integration examples, practical guidance and relevant materials openly available so other organisations can adapt and extend them.
- **Enable community participation and continuity:** Allow external contributors to propose opportunities, contribute improvements and continue adoption efforts using existing ValOS infrastructure, without depending on Lionscraft.

**The result is an open, reusable body of adoption work that grows with each contribution.** Every adoption can make the next easier, while helping the Ethereum ecosystem independently expand, maintain and improve the use of ValOS.
sections.out_scope:
- Performing audits, security assessments or certification.
- Operating or securing third-party validator infrastructure.
- Building or maintaining partners' security products or services.
- Creating new assurance, ratings or certification standards.
- Routine ValOS governance, standards maintenance or publication of ValOS v2.
- Funding or administering existing Lido assessment subsidies.
- Adoption outside the Ethereum ecosystem.

criteria: A further 3 distinct, independent professional Ethereum node operators running mainnet validators complete ValOS self-assessments or independent assessments, bringing cumulative verified operator adoptions to at least 6.

revisions.title: ValOS: Keep ETH InfraOps Open, Secure & Resilient

- **Maintain an open adoption register:** Publish opportunities, their proposed ValOS applications, progress, obstacles and next steps, so others can participate or pursue them independently.
- **Document adoption work as it happens:** Share outreach approaches, integration methods, decisions, outcomes and lessons learned, including unsuccessful efforts, while protecting confidential and security-sensitive information.
- **Publish reusable adoption resources:** Make non-confidential integration examples, practical guidance and relevant materials openly available so other organisations can adapt and extend them.
- **Enable community participation and continuity:** Allow external contributors to propose opportunities, contribute improvements and continue adoption efforts using existing ValOS infrastructure, without depending on Lionscraft.

**The result is an open, reusable body of adoption work that grows with each contribution.** Every adoption can make the next easier, while helping the Ethereum ecosystem independently expand, maintain and improve the use of ValOS.
sections.out_scope:
- Performing audits, security assessments or certification.
- Operating or securing third-party validator infrastructure.
- Building or maintaining partners' security products or services.
- Creating new assurance, ratings or certification standards.
- Routine ValOS governance, standards maintenance or publication of ValOS v2.
- Funding or administering existing Lido assessment subsidies.
- Adoption outside the Ethereum ecosystem.
sections.team:
**[Lionscraft](https://www.lionscraft.io/) has been the lead contributor, coordinator and maintainer of D.U.C.K. and subsequently ValOS since the initiative began in 2023.** Over nearly three years, Lionscraft has led the development, publication and ongoing improvement of the standard, its security controls, tools and best practices.

The initiative has involved contributions from 20 organisations across Ethereum staking, node operations, cybersecurity, risk and assurance. Lionscraft coordinated their participation, bringing together organisations with different expertise and levels of involvement. Some were major contributors to the standard and its supporting resources, while others provided specialist input, reviewed specific sections or contributed to individual controls and practices.

This experience is directly relevant to VOAP. Lionscraft has already demonstrated its ability to coordinate diverse independent organisations around a shared, open-source security framework, manage contributions and turn that collaboration into published outputs. **VOAP builds on this experience, shifting the focus from developing ValOS to driving its adoption across the Ethereum ecosystem.**
sections.why_grant:
**ValOS is the result of nearly three years of development and industry collaboration, originally initiated and funded through Lido.**

Beginning with D.U.C.K. in November 2023, the initiative evolved through two phases of development, delivering an open-source security standard, risk and controls framework, assessment resources, toolkits and best practices for Ethereum validator operations. The full ValOS standard launched in September 2026.

The work has already delivered:

- **An open-source standard:** Published security risks, controls, mitigation practices and assessment guidance, available for anyone to use, adapt and extend.
- **Tools and best practices:** Existing resources that support operators in assessing and improving their security and resilience.
- **Industry collaboration:** Contributions from 20 organisations across staking operations, exchanges, cybersecurity, risk and assurance.
- **An independent assessment pathway:** Qualified third-party assessors can evaluate operators against ValOS. Lido will also subsidise part of the assessment costs for four early-adopter node operators.

With the standard, toolkits and best practices now established, the next phase is accelerating adoption across the wider Ethereum ecosystem.

VOAP will leverage existing resources, relationships and adoption pathways to minimise programme overhead and concentrate resources on real-world implementation. Of the $78,000 funding request, $34,000 is directly contingent upon independently verified operational adoption outcomes.

**Public documentation and prior work:** The initiative's development history is documented in the [original D.U.C.K. proposal on Lido Research](https://research.lido.fi/t/d-u-c-k-distributed-utilization-of-configurations-and-knowledge-proposal/5848), with its first published framework available in the [D.U.C.K. Knowledge Base](https://duck-initiative.gitbook.io/d.u.c.k.-knowledge-base). The subsequent development phase is documented in the [ValOS governance, assurance and adoption proposal](https://research.lido.fi/t/strengthen-d-u-c-k-governance-assurance-and-real-world-adoption/9849/4). Lido's continuing support for independent assessments is documented in the [early-adopter assessment subsidy proposal](https://research.lido.fi/t/proposal-funding-request-for-valos-early-adopter-assessment-subsidies/10657). The resulting open-source standard and its development history are available in the [ValOS GitHub repository](https://github.com/lidofinance/valos).
sections.commitments:
- **Operational security adoption:** Drive real-world implementation of ValOS security controls among Ethereum infrastructure operators and integration into existing security and assurance services.
- **Verifiable adoption:** Deliver at least 12 independently verifiable operational adoptions across 9 professional Ethereum node operators and 3 security and assurance providers.
- **Diverse adoption:** Achieve operational adoption across operators of different sizes and staking affiliations, including at least 4 operators with at least 10,000 ETH staked each, at least 3 operators with fewer than 10,000 ETH staked each, and at least 3 Lido node operators, as specified in the adoption milestones.
- **Outcome-based funding:** Allocate $34,000, representing 43.6% of the requested funding, directly to independently verified operational adoption milestones.
- **Open adoption:** Publicly document adoption opportunities, approaches, progress, outcomes and lessons learned, making non-confidential materials openly available for others to reuse and extend.
- **Security and resilience continuity:** Ensure VOAP-supported adoptions address how operational security controls, assessments and assurance will be maintained, reviewed and improved over time.
- **Independent verification:** Provide evidence of completed adoption milestones for independent review, while protecting confidential information and security-sensitive findings.
- **Long-term sustainability:** Enable adopting organisations to maintain their own implementations and allow the wider Ethereum community to continue adoption efforts through existing ValOS infrastructure, independently of Lionscraft.

milestones.name: Activate ValOS Adoption
criteria: Identify at least 20 qualified prospective adopters across Ethereum's staking and security and assurance ecosystems, each with a specific ValOS security or resilience application; the independent reviewer verifies prospect records.
Deliver individualised ValOS adoption approaches to organisations in the initial pool, identifying the application and next action; the reviewer verifies dated correspondence.

milestones.name: Drive Staking Ecosystem Adoption
criteria: Deliver at least 10 documented operator-specific adoption actions involving ValOS self-assessment, independent assessment or ongoing security and resilience practices; the independent reviewer inspects correspondence and activity records.

Deliver at least 3 tailored proposals to staking protocols, pools or institutional stakers explaining how ValOS evidence could inform operator oversight, selection or incentives; the reviewer verifies proposals and delivery records.

milestones.name: Drive Security & Assurance Ecosystem Adoption
criteria: Deliver at least 10 documented provider-specific adoption actions involving real ValOS applications in assurance, ratings, monitoring, infrastructure security or financial risk services; the independent reviewer checks correspondence and activity records.

Deliver at least 3 tailored provider proposals describing a specific ValOS integration, relevant security risks and a partner-owned mechanism for continued assessment, monitoring or review; the reviewer verifies delivery records.

milestones.name: Staking Ecosystem Operational Adoption — First 3 Operators
criteria: At least 3 distinct, independent professional Ethereum node operators running mainnet validators complete ValOS self-assessments or independent assessments, including at least 1 operator with at least 10,000 ETH staked.

Each operator incorporates relevant ValOS controls into its security-management processes and identifies responsibility for continued control review; the independent reviewer verifies assessment completion and supporting records.

milestones.name: Staking Ecosystem Operational Adoption — Second Set of 3 Operators
criteria: At least 6 total distinct, independent professional Ethereum node operators running mainnet validators complete ValOS self-assessments or independent assessments, including at least 2 operators with at least 10,000 ETH staked each, at least 2 operators with fewer than 10,000 ETH staked each, and at least 1 Lido node operator.

Each operator incorporates relevant ValOS controls into its security-management processes and identifies responsibility for continued control review; the independent reviewer verifies assessment completion and supporting records.

milestones.name: Staking Ecosystem Operational Adoption — Third Set of 3 Operators
criteria: At least 9 total distinct, independent professional Ethereum node operators running mainnet validators complete ValOS self-assessments or independent assessments, including at least 4 operators with at least 10,000 ETH staked each, at least 3 operators with fewer than 10,000 ETH staked each, and at least 3 Lido node operators.

Each operator incorporates relevant ValOS controls into its security-management processes and identifies responsibility for continued control review; the independent reviewer verifies assessment completion and supporting records.

milestones.name: Security & Assurance Ecosystem Operational Adoption — First 3 Providers
criteria: At least 3 distinct security and assurance providers operationally integrate ValOS into existing services, products or repeatable processes, covering at least 2 different application areas such as independent assessment, ratings, security monitoring, infrastructure security or financial risk services.
